{'text': 'In the history of technology, the partnership between Steve Jobs and Jony Ive can be considered one of the most famous and successful collaborations. After Tim Cook took over as CEO, he did not play the same role as Jobs did in working with Ive on hardware design—and that was the right call.', 'isTranslationSuccessful': True}

{'text': "John Ternus appears to have taken a more Steve-like approach, getting close to Apple's design division, and I believe that's equally the right move…", 'isTranslationSuccessful': True}

{'text': "Many of Apple's most iconic designs came from the unique partnership between Steve Jobs and Jony. The two worked very closely together, typically meeting at least once a day, and the results were far better than either could have achieved alone.", 'isTranslationSuccessful': True}

{'text': 'Both of them wanted to push the boundaries of hardware design, and both took an extremely meticulous and detailed approach. However, their primary focuses were different. Ive was obsessed with making hardware as thin and minimal as possible, while Steve was equally obsessed with delivering the best user experience.', 'isTranslationSuccessful': True}

{'text': 'Although Ive often said that design is about far more than just appearance, he had a reputation for prioritising form over function, which led to problematic design issues like the butterfly keyboard, and the prevailing view is that Steve played a crucial role during his lifetime in counterbalancing that tendency.', 'isTranslationSuccessful': True}

{'text': "After Cook took over as CEO, he reportedly took a noticeably more hands-off approach to the company's design team, visiting the design division roughly only once a month. Given that Cook's expertise is in operations and people management, that made complete sense.", 'isTranslationSuccessful': True}

{'text': "That's not to say Cook didn't make useful contributions, but if he had been too deeply involved in design decisions—especially at the earlier stages—it would likely have backfired. In particular, his obsession with costs could have held back the team's ambitions.", 'isTranslationSuccessful': True}

{'text': 'By contrast, Ternus is a hardware person through and through. Before becoming CEO, he had essentially taken over the hardware engineering leadership role previously held by Ive, and Apple has praised his important role in the development of the iPad and AirPods product lines before Ive left the company.', 'isTranslationSuccessful': True}

{'text': "Ternus is said to be, like Steve, someone who steps in to correct situations where flashy aesthetics are prioritised over practicality. Although the current design pairing of Molly Anderson and Steve Lemay is clearly highly effective, one element of that successful formula seems to be precisely Ternus's oversight.", 'isTranslationSuccessful': True}

{'text': "I'm personally very glad to hear that Ternus continues to prioritise this work even as his time becomes more stretched. The Anderson-Lemay-Ternus team is working very well together, and I hope it can continue that way.", 'isTranslationSuccessful': True}
